0.original: Wuk Lamat is eager to attempt the next feat.

24.original: Speak with Wuk Lamat and have her accompany you.

25.original: Speak with Ropli while Wuk Lamat is accompanying you.

48.original: I have not forgotten our obligations to Wuk Lamat, but it's moments like these─when we can immerse ourselves in the cultures of others─that fill me with anticipation for the new experiences this adventure will bring us.

49.original: We've made a good start on these challenges. Hopefully we can keep it up.

50.original: In a contest like this one, 'tis only a matter of time until the claimants are pitted against each other in direct competition.

51.original: Traveling with so large and diverse a group is...unfamiliar to me. If she could see me now...

52.original: We've now won keystones from both the Feat of Reeds and the Feat of Gold. Surely that means our approach to the contest was the right one?

53.original: So it would seem. By continuing to retrace Gulool Ja Ja's journey as presented in the saga, we should find the remaining electors in turn.

54.original: Then let's visit the giants next! Like Krile said, the fact that they were searching for the golden city might mean they know something useful.

55.original: The home of the Yok Huy is in the upper reaches of Urqopacha. Unless you're keen on scaling the cliffs, we'll have to take the long way around─through Kozama'uka.

56.original: This route will take us close to the Moblin village...which is another important location in the saga.

57.original: Since we'll need all the keystones eventually, it makes sense to pay them a visit while we're passing through.

58.original: So we call on the Moblins first, then. Let's head there right now!

59.original: I'm afraid “right now” is going to be a problem...

60.original: The Flight of We Wingless, the great stairs leading to the Moblin settlement, collapsed in the storm.

61.original: What are we to do, then?

62.original: There is an alternative, but it requires preparation. Until it's ready, you could rest at the cabins or see more of the city. Whatever you prefer.

63.original: Just to be sure: you'll accept <hex:021A020203>any<hex:021A020103> method of travel as long as it gets us to our destination?

64.original: Of course. Who do you take me for?

65.original: ...Hmm. Then as your guide, I will see to the arrangements.

66.original: Well, it seems we have some free time on our hands. Let us make the most of it.

67.original: I need to get my axe repaired. I nicked the blade pretty badly when I took a swing at Bakool Ja Ja.

68.original: That reminds me, I never got around to introducing you to Ropli, did I? He's the man in charge of Wachumeqimeqi, and a good person to know. Want to come along?

70.original: Ready? The markets of Wachumeqimeqi are to the east, on the other side of Bayside Bevy.

71.original: Wuk Lamat is now accompanying you. Keep her at your side in order to proceed with quest objectives.

72.original: You can leave Wuk Lamat behind by entering a different area, or by speaking with her and selecting the option to part ways.

73.original: If you wish to have Wuk Lamat accompany you again, return and speak with her at the original location.

79.original: Wachumeqimeqi is everything that Tuliyollal was built to be.

80.original: This is Aunt Tii's Tacos, named for its owner here, the lovely Tiisol.

81.original: If you're after the best tacos in Tuliyollal, this place sits at the top with Xbalyav Ty'e.

82.original: You say that, Third Promise, but you only ever eat old Br'uk Evu's food! Come and buy mine for a change!

83.original: Sorry, Tiisol! It has been a while, hasn't it? I swear I'll stop for a bite once the contest is over.

84.original: Are you sure you wish to part ways with your companion?

85.original: Something you eat not agree with you? Well, I'll be waiting by Xbalyav Ty'e whenever you're ready!

86.original: Feeling better? Let's get back to it, then!

87.original: Apologies, but I'm rather busy at the moment. Please come back later.

88.original: You should have Wuk Lamat accompanying you before continuing.

89.original: Wuk Lamat has yet to arrive. Be sure she is at your side before attempting to continue.

90.original: My, my, the Third Promise. How might I assist you this fine <hex:020839E3E90C0DFF1B020817E3E90C05FF086576656E696E67FF086D6F726E696E6703FF17020813E3E90C12FF04646179FF086576656E696E670303>?

91.original: Well met, Ropli! I need to buff a nasty nick out of my axe blade.

92.original: Yes, it's been chipped quite terribly. Trying to cleave rocks again, were we?

93.original: Er, something like that. Think you can fix it?

94.original: You stand among Tural's most prestigious gathering of artisans and ask this question? 'Tis child's play. We'll have it repaired for you in two shakes of an alpaca's tail.

95.original: Good to hear! I leave it in your capable hands.

96.original: Who's your companion, if I may ask?

97.original: This is <hex:022C0DFF07022903EB0203FF02200203>, a great adventurer I recruited from across the salt!

98.original: I brought <hex:02080DE905FF04686572FF0468696D03> here to meet you, actually. Thought <hex:02080CE905FF04736865FF03686503> might have reason to visit Wachumeqimeqi sooner or later.

99.original: Then allow me to introduce myself. I am Ropli, humble representative of this grand center of trade. A pleasure to meet you, <hex:022C0DFF07022903EB0203FF02200203>.

100.original: You there! Stop dithering in the shadows and announce your business already!

101.original: Hrm, I've seen that man somewhere before...

102.original: A jewelry maker you met on the voyage over?

103.original: Oh, I remember─I spoke with him, too! Fonjean...taine? Yes, that was his name!

104.original: You've been loitering like a flighty admirer who can't pluck up the courage to confess his feelings. Out with it, then. Why are you here?

105.original: I, uh... That is to say...

106.original: <sigh> And we're no closer to solving that enigma.

107.original: Hrm, I wonder if he could use someone to talk to... I say we go and ask! Let me know by linkpearl if you find him first.

108.original: Our nervous man of mystery fled westwards...never to be seen again?

109.original: You were conversing with Master Ropli... But wait─we've met before, haven't we? On the ship...

110.original: You've found him? Good, I'll be right there!

111.original: Why did you run off like that? Did you have business with Ropli or not?

112.original: Please, you needn't concern yourselves with my affairs! I'm undeserving of such attention!

113.original: Huh? What are you going on about?

114.original: I beg of you, do not ask me to explain! Do not!

115.original: Sorry, but the more you tell me not to, the more curious I become. Besides, you look like you need a friend.

116.original: <sigh> You are too kind... So be it. I suppose I can share with you a morsel of my misery...

117.original: Before I came to Tuliyollal, I worked as a goldsmith at the most prestigious jewelry maker in all of Ul'dah─Eshtaime's Aesthetics. Oh, it started off well enough, but as the days passed, everything began to go wrong!

118.original: Compared to the masterpieces of my talented colleagues, my products were lacking. <hex:021A020203>Mediocre<hex:021A020103>! I lost all confidence. Crippling doubt had possessed me, and any veneer of bravado I tried to put forth soon cracked beneath its weight!

119.original: Thus did I take ship, hoping to find a fresh beginning on new shores. Yet as you witnessed, I lack the courage to even approach a potential employer. You stand before a man wallowing in the wreckage of his ill-spent existence!

120.original: Uh...alright, then. You offered a “morsel,” then served us the full course.

121.original: You must've <hex:021A020203>really<hex:021A020103> wanted someone to hear your story. If you like, I could try to give you a few words of advice.

122.original: Then...you have experience with my predicament? Of feeling terribly inadequate compared to your undeniably superior peers?

123.original: Well...when you put it that way, I, uh...

124.original: Ah...hahaha, not me! I'm Wuk Lamat, Third Promise of Tuliyollal!

126.original: O-Oh, of course, you're a member of the royal family! Please forgive my presumptuousness!

127.original: But what of you? Have you ever measured your work against that of your colleagues and found yourself wanting...?

129.original: You can't measure your worth by the success of others.

131.original: How can I not? Should my work not meet the same exacting standards, no new commissions will be forthcoming! What then was the point of my becoming a goldsmith...?

132.original: If even an ally handpicked by the Third Promise can feel such doubt, then what hope is there for me? I must question why I bothered to become a goldsmith in the first place...

133.original: Hmmm... Looking back, 'twas my father who inspired me to take up the trade. His exquisite creations brought radiant smiles to the faces of his clients, and I admired him deeply for it.

134.original: But in the course of striving to be as great a goldsmith as him, I lost sight of my original motivation...

135.original: All I ever wanted was to spread joy through my craft, as he did.

136.original: Perhaps...perhaps I will give this one last try. Thank you both for reminding me of what is truly important!

139.original: Oh, sorry, <hex:022C0DFF07022903EB0203FF02200203>! I didn't mean to ignore you.

140.original: But, yes─I'm glad to see Fonjeantaine is giving himself another chance!
